creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Fencil decision pane-headers (owner-nodded, 2026-11-08), drawn on the window board of the Lectern page muster-ui-redesign.

Each pane gets a header with its chord, state icon, callsign, name, directory, state word and time held, and context bar. Blocked and stuck headers are tinted, as the agent list's rows are. A split then says which agent is which without the sidebar.

- Panes stay flush, with today's divider and no gaps or rounded corners between them. The mock-up's gaps cost space the owner wants for text, and headers do not need them, so a header costs only its own height, about one line.
- The border marks only the pane the keyboard reaches; the state-colored border goes. docs/architecture.md describes that border legend and changes with it.
- Colors come from the color card beside this one (decision chrome-colors): the header is the pane's background shifted toward its foreground.
- No setting turns headers off. The owner may want one after using them; build it then, not ahead of his verdict.

## Plan (reviewed 2026-11-08)

From the plan for the redesign, step 7; the parent card a_2wKW8eBfM has its overall shape, order and checks.

`PaneChrome.layout()` is the one place that sets a pane's surface frame, and libghostty sizes the
PTY from that frame. The core sends only split ratios, so nothing in the core changes.

- `PaneChrome` gains a header view, 24 pt, flush at the top. `surface.frame` loses the header height
  as well as the focus inset; nothing else is needed for the PTY to get the right size.
- The state border goes. `layer.borderWidth` is used only for the focus ring, and the header's tint
  and edge carry blocked and stuck.
- A pane shorter than 60 pt draws no header, since `PaneTree.minimumPaneSize` is 8 pt and a header
  would otherwise leave the terminal a negative height.
- The drag handle moves into the header: the whole header is the drag band. `PaneDragTests`, which
  pin the handle's frame and band, change with it.
- The find bar and the paste label position themselves against `surface.frame` rather than the
  pane's bounds, so they stay out of the header.
- Docs and tests that describe the state border change in the same commit: `docs/architecture.md`
  ("The two rings differ in kind"), `docs/configuration.md` (`agent_*` paint "a pane's edge"), the
  `PaneChrome` class comment, and `theRingsDifferInKind` in `PaneChromeTests`. The default color
  table and its tripwire stay; the colors are unchanged.
title: Pane headers carry chord, state and directory; panes stay flush; the border marks only focus
